key_insight: A three-level optimization chain—matrix SVD, block-level joint refinement, and end-to-end loss tuning—beats independent per-matrix compression because local optimality does not prevent nonlinear error accumulation in Transformer blocks.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical low-rank LLM compression recipe that can improve perplexity at high compression rates using only a small calibration set and no instruction or recovery data.
method: Whiten each matrix and apply truncated SVD (L1).
Jointly optimize compressed matrices within each Transformer block (L2).
Refine the compressed model end-to-end on language modeling loss (L3).
evidence_signal: On LLaMA-7B at 60% compression, WikiText-2 perplexity improved from 42.1 to 19.1 to 11.4 across the three stages, with results reported on 256 calibration sequences and tests across 20–80% compression and multiple model families.
watch_item: The reported gains are primarily perplexity/compression-fidelity improvements; downstream task accuracy remains below the dense model, and cross-architecture results use architecture-specific settings.
paper_title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression
